title: A Gravity for the Vector
premise: Hazel Eastwick, a terraformer and cargo hauler in the contested orbits of Kepler Station, discovers a ghost manifest: a ship that never flew, carrying a passenger name that shouldn't exist — their own birth name, given up seven years ago. The manifest is bait, planted by the station's ruling consortium to flush out dissenters among the cryosleep crews who must choose which half of humanity wakes before the jump window closes. As Hazel's found family of haulers fractures under consortium pressure, loyalty and truth pull in opposite directions, and Hazel realizes the garden they tend is the consortium's insurance policy, not humanity's. In the end, Hazel broadcasts the true manifest to every sleeping ship, splits the jump window with the other half of humanity rather than choosing for them, and loses the station — but keeps the family that chose to stay.
about_author: B. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing routing algorithms for orbital freight before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where they keep an improbable garden and insist the best science fiction is about paperwork gone wrong.

chapters.title: The Manifest of a Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Hazel Eastwick's POV. While logging cargo for the consortium's dormant fleet, Hazel finds a manifest for the Vesperine — a hauler scrapped years ago — listing a passenger under the name they abandoned on Earth. They pull their found family of dockhands and pilots into the mystery, and the emotional beat is unease: the past has a paper trail, and someone wants it found.

chapters.title: Everything the Garden Was For
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Hazel and Idris, the station's aging cryosleep engineer and Hazel's mentor. Investigating the ghost manifest, Hazel discovers the seed vault beneath their terraform garden is coded to wake only one hemisphere's sleepers — the consortium's chosen half. Idris confesses he helped design the filter. The beat is betrayal inside loyalty: family, it turns out, keeps secrets too.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating through the crew. The consortium moves up the jump window by six days, forcing the wake-list to lock. Crew members are offered amnesty for naming Hazel; one takes it. Hazel is detained in the Vesperine's sealed hold — the ship that never flew, made real as a prison. The beat is fracture: the found family bends, and Hazel must decide whether truth is worth the people it costs.

chapters.title: A Gravity for the Vector
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with a closing passage from the garden itself. Freed by the crewmate who betrayed them, Hazel broadcasts the unfiltered manifest to every sleeping ship and overrides the vault filter, splitting the jump window so both halves of humanity wake. The station is stripped from them; the crew scatters but regathers at a smaller dock, planting the garden's seeds anew. The beat is costly, chosen hope.
